keyVerseText: Salute Apelles approved in Christ. Salute them which are of Aristobulus' household. household: or, friends
rootMeaning: The name Ἀπελλῆς (Apellēs) is of Latin origin, which suggests it was likely adopted into the Greek-speaking Christian community from a Roman cultural background. Since no root word or further etymology is provided, the literal sense of the name itself does not carry a specific meaning beyond identifying a person. This personal name, therefore, serves primarily as a proper noun, distinguishing an individual within the early Christian context rather than conveying a conceptual or thematic meaning.
usageInScripture: The word Ἀπελλῆς appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Romans 16:10, where it is translated simply as 'Apelles.' This singular occurrence indicates that the term functions solely as a proper name, identifying a particular Christian individual. The consistency in translation as a personal name underscores its role as a reference to a person rather than a descriptive term or title.
theologicalSignificance: Although Ἀπελλῆς is simply a personal name, its presence in Scripture highlights the importance of individual believers within the body of Christ. The mention of Apelles as 'approved in Christ' signifies the recognition and affirmation of faithful Christians in the early church. This reminds us that God values each believer personally and publicly, encouraging us to live lives worthy of such commendation. It also reflects the unity of diverse cultural backgrounds within the church, as a Latin-origin name appears in a Greek text, symbolizing the universal nature of the gospel.
keyVerseReflection: Romans 16:10 says, 'Salute Apelles approved in Christ.' The use of the name Apelles here personalizes the greeting, emphasizing the commendation of this individual as one who is tested and found faithful in Christ. The word Ἀπελλῆς anchors the verse in real community relationships, reminding readers that the apostle Paul recognized and honored genuine believers by name. This personal acknowledgment encourages believers today to seek approval in Christ through faithful living.
